title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed Bourbaki draft: the header reads '6 - 26 -' and 'n° 392', which is a Bourbaki rédaction number. It contains exercises for the chapter on divisors (Algèbre commutative ch. VII, 'Diviseurs', §3 on factorial rings). The sheet was presumably reused as scrap paper for, or filed among, Grothendieck's handwritten notes. The neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on averaging and invariants of representations of groups with a unipotent open subgroup. Those concern ℓ-adic or Galois representations for the L-function notes.

Content of the page:

(1) End of exercise 8. This is Samuel's construction of a factorial ring A whose formal power series ring A[[T]] is not factorial. The data are A built from x, y, z with a relation of type x^i + y^j + z^k = 0 (or a similar trinomial), with exponents i, j, k. Part a) ends with a hint: inside each interval take b_{n+1} = b_n z^{i-1} x^{-1}; at the endpoints use ijk − ij − jk − ki ≥ 0, i.e. 1/i + 1/j + 1/k ≤ 1. Part b): if z^{i-1} ∉ Ax + Ay, no series in A[[T]] with constant term y^k is associate to v in B[[T]]. Here B is a completion. The proof compares the coefficient of T. Part c) combines this with exercise 7, which gives factoriality of A, to show A[[T]] is not factorial. The argument: vv' cannot be a product of extremal (prime) factors u_h. One passes to C = S'^{-1}A[[T]], a Zariski ring whose completion is B[[T]], and obtains a contradiction with b). Part d) deduces a factorial noetherian local ring whose completion is a Krull ring that is not factorial.

(2) Exercise 9. Let A be a noetherian domain whose localizations at maximal ideals are DVRs (a Dedekind ring). Then every localization of B = A[[X_1,…,X_n]] at a maximal ideal is factorial, via its completion and a proposition 8 of n° 9. Hence divisorial ideals of B are projective. If finitely generated projective C-modules are free, the same holds for C[[X]]. Therefore A[[X_1,…,X_n]] is factorial for A a PID.

(3) Exercise 10: a factorial Prüfer ring is principal, and a pseudo-Bézout Krull ring is factorial.

(4) Exercise 11: K[X,Y] ∩ K(X², Y/X) is not factorial.

All of this is standard commutative algebra of 1961–65. It serves Bourbaki's treatment of unique factorization, not the L-function project of the surrounding notes.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible on this excerpt. The full hypotheses on x, y, z, i, j, k are on the previous page of the Bourbaki draft, which is not included, so they cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: A factorial (even complete local) ring A with A[[T]] not factorial, using a trinomial relation and the condition 1/i + 1/j + 1/k ≤ 1
ideas.modern_name: Samuel's counterexample to factoriality of power series rings
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Samuel (1961, 'On unique factorization domains'; Tata lectures 1964)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative ch. VII, §3 exercises (1965)

ideas.what: A[[X_1..X_n]] is factorial for A a PID, via local factoriality and 'projective implies free' passing to C[[X]]
ideas.modern_name: Factoriality of power series over a PID (or over a regular UFD of dimension ≤ 2)

ideas.what: A factorial Prüfer ring is principal; a pseudo-Bézout Krull ring is factorial
ideas.modern_name: Standard characterizations of PIDs and UFDs

ideas.what: The intersection of a UFD with a subfield need not be factorial: K[X,Y] ∩ K(X², Y/X)
ideas.modern_name: Non-factorial ring of invariants / intersection example
